data.name: Syndrome
data.detailed_description:
WISHLIST BENEATH - UPCOMING ACTION/HORROR GAME


Acerca do jogo

Acordas atordoado e confuso, provavelmente devido aos efeitos do criosono.
Não encontras ninguém, mas rapidamente começas a encontrar os corpos da tua tripulação.
A nave está à deriva, e quem - ou o quê - matou os teus colegas, ainda está provavelmente à solta.

Syndrome é um jogo de survival horror de ficção científica, que tem lugar abordo da "Valkenburg", uma nave de exploração e ciência equipada com os sitemas mais avançados da frota da Novacore.

Precisas de descobrir o que aconteceu com a tua tripulação, e fazer o que for preciso para sobreviver a este pesadelo.
Os inimigos são poderosos e numerosos, o que significa que discrição é provavelmente a melhor estratégia.
Vais encontrar armas na nave, mas as munições são muito escassas e devem ser usadas prudentemente.

CARACTERÍSTICAS


● Terror claustrofóbico: a acção tem lugar dentro duma nave espacial. Há horrores incontáveis lá dentro, tanto físicos como psicológicos.

● Combater ou esconder: há armas na nave, mas não há munições suficientes para enfrentar todos os inimigos. Usa as munições com cautela.

● História envolvente: nada é o que parece. Algo de muito mau aconteceu a bordo da nave, e cabe-te a ti perceber o que se está realmente a passar.

● Inimigos reactivos: os inimigos vão seguir os barulhos e investigar quaisquer distúrbios.

● Cenário interactivo: há muito para explorar dentro da nave, e muitas coisas para descobrir.

reviews.review:
I can't say I'm terribly impressed... 
The controls were waxy and slow to respond. Crouching was possibly the slowest I can recall from any game (and instantly makes your camera feel like you're drunk with how it sways)
The player having the stamina of an anaemic 90 year old wasn't much fun. Especially when so much of this game is a walking simulator.
The character felt too short too... I'm walking up to doors with a 'window' and I can't even see through that window. I got the whole experience of being five foot tall, weak, slow and feeble all in one package.
The levels were pointlessly dark with severe changes in contrast (so many reflective surfaces and yet a billion-lumen LED will only illuminate a square inch around itself). 
The first enemies were both slow, and damage-sponges, while attacking faster than me and spawning endlessly apparently (when there's only one way in and out of a place, this is rather irritating).
When I saw a different enemy, it was fast... and otherwise identical in attack pattern to the first lot I'd been borg'd by.
Most of the 'horror' comes from having endless sounds playing, but the law of diminishing returns kind of kills that in ten minutes. Tapping? Right, heard it. Probably not an enemy then. Creaking? Yep. Random scream? That was scary before I heard it thirty times when just trying to walk around this place.
Oh, unless you count having the max HP of a butterfly and healing items that don't do much more than a band-aid, but that's less horror and more 'Don't waste my last ten minutes of WALKING AROUND FROM OBJECTIVE TO OBJECTIVE BY KILLING ME!' 

'oh no, it might get me' is meant to be a good way to instil fear. 'oh great. One of these things can and will kill me because there is one save-point on the whole floor and I have to literally walk from one end of it to the other three times for three objectives.' is just boring.

There's no feeling of exploration, since the only place you can go is your next objective, or previously opened doors. You're very quickly railroaded into 'do this. Then this. Then this'.
There's probably a deeper story going on, but frankly, I fear I will come up with something better if I try to imagine it.
"Trust nobody on this ship, I don't... now let me tell you exactly what to do, how to do it and while I'm at it, not tell you anything else" is basically the script of the second person you hear from.

Attacking is slow, stamina-expensive and ineffective.
The enemies CAN be killed, but it will cost about half your health since blocking is...
...
...
...
SLOW!
We get 'THE TOOL' a little into the first chapter... Space-monkey wrench... for the spaghetti arms of our player, it does a shameful amount of damage (and I have only fought the fleshy things).
Nice to see that it's a maintenance device to overcome that one obstacle of opening a vent, but now it's for prodding things slower than they can slap you six shades of space-silly.

There's no impressive introduction for the first enemy, it is just 'there' walking towards you as you bumble around to find yet another place. The character's freakout is not unfair, but then doesn't seem to go away. "they're coming, run!" uuh, no. I need to do the thing I'm almost at the room for. THEN run the five feet I am able to before my stamina runs out... before walking casually back to the elevator, checking my map often, eating four sandwiches, two drinks and a heap of cookies. Gee, good thing I'm safe in the only elevator on this whole ship.

OOPS, I stepped on a cable. I guess I'll just eat half my healing items to heal that... Shame things like rubber don't exist to make our shoes out of. (I'm assuming this cable is hot, because if it's electric, then we're all dead since EVERYTHING is made of metal apparently.)

I know this isn't NASA, but the 'one elevator' thing only works if it looks like it was even designed that way. There's no centralised elevator access, It looks like a service elevator for when the stairs break down!
Is each floor self-contained until... people magically appear wherever they sleep and eat? I will ignore the toilets in space argument, but there is some serious suspension of disbelief going on.

The nightmare scenes are interesting, but without being able to tell what it's saying, I'm getting 'ominous growl, hiss, thing that sounded like 'why' and then the character is telling me it's voices'.

Space-faring, yet we can't manage emergency lighting. Sure. Artificial gravity, but we still have random vents that gush steam at shoulder-height. Space-boxes covered in lights, but we can't have a flashlight that doesn't take batteries, or illuminates more than a dime.
Hang on, I need to get into any room with a blocked door, good thing they're the only ones with vents leading to them.
Thank goodness we have holographic technology to tell us when doors are locked. Shame we don't know about fire extinguishers!
Wow, AI tech and robots... What do you mean someone made a 'hacking device' that magically unlocks terminals after matching four symbols.

I'm not sure I'd want to know what this ship is meant to look like seeing how different the only two floors I saw was.
"I'm clearly on a maintenance floor since everything looks brown with extra beams and angled walls", "Oh look, I'm in a science area, with the only spiral staircase in the game..."

I know that making a game is hard... but this feels a LOT like a PS2 game, and I am sadly not being complimentary here.
It looks like it was designed to be 'as horror as possible' while totally forgetting that anything is meant to work. Medical is... just down this complicated series of corridors, only accessible on one floor, only accessible from one lift. What if someone burns themselves on this FACE-HEIGHT STEAM VENT' while not on floor 5?
Countless odd-looking bleep-bloops and devices which, even if whoever we're playing as cannot use them, at least can acknowledge that they're heavy and would do damage if thrown hard enough at, say, that slowly-approaching borgposter?

An hour and a half and the first time I died, I'm actually glad so I can justify turning all this off.
I lost about twenty minutes of gameplay, walking from the save-point to the elevator, across the whole floor to interact with one thing, back to the elevator, back to NEAR the save-point... only to be killed by two borg who were just chilling by the door I needed to go through. Couldn't hit them fast enough, or time any kind of blocks, so thankfully I died.

I feel I'm seriously missing something here, but honestly, there's too much that I can't ignore about how this game plays to continue.
